episodes.178340: Very warm spring temperatures and an above normal snowpack resulted in excessive runoff leading to mud and debris flows across portions of west-central Colorado, as well as damage due to flooding.
episodes.178429: A shower produced strong wind gusts over portions of Tangier Sound.
episodes.178545: Well above average snowpack and warm temperatures led to rapid snowmelt and river rises on many northern NM river basins. Overbank flooding was reported at and downstream of the junction between the Rio Ojo Caliente and Rio Chama between May 5th and May 10th. Ten properties had water up to homes and structures. Yards, wells, and septic systems were flooded out. There were no reports of casualties or fatalities or water rescues.
episodes.180312: A strong upper level low pressure system along with a weak shortwave trough moved into Eastern Oregon during the early afternoon. This system brought strong and long lasting rotating thunderstorms that caused severe wind damage.
episodes.180626: A negatively-tilted, shortwave trough across the Four Corners brought lee troughing across the Southern Plains. A dryline was positioned across portions of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. Many splitting supercells developed along the dryline, producing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180921: A low that settled into the west coast the first few days of May brought showers and an increased chance (20-30%) of thunderstorms that also lowered rain-snow lines to 5500-7000 feet by early morning 3 May. Stronger showers and storms produced a mix of rain, snow, and ice pellets which lead to runoff issues in the lower elevations. High end chances (10-20%) of rainfall totals were expected to reach 0.50-1.00 inch. Although snow was projected to fall in the Sierra, the combination of warm road temperatures and the early May sun angle limited accumulations on paved surfaces. But bursts of convective heavy snow showers and/or snow occurring during the overnight hours were expected to bring overnight travel impacts to mountain passes. Tightening thermal and pressure gradients with the incoming low produced gusty south-southeast winds and travel impacts for portions of Churchill, Mineral, Lyon, and Mono Counties along US-395 and US-95.

events.narrative: A couple of trees were knocked down on Pine Creek Road.
A trained spotter near Drewsey, OR reported a blown down willow tree and small hail.
The mesonet station ATFO3 at Antelope measured a 53 knot wind gust.
A large mudslide occurred as a result of rapid snowmelt on County Road 129 south of Clark near Fetcher Ranch.

events.county: Tangier Sound And The Inland Waters Surrounding Bloodsworth Island
events.narrative: A wind gust of 44 knots (51 MPH) was measured by the Crisfield WeatherFlow sensor (XCRS).
Minor flooding was observed in early May at Thatcher L&D on the Ouachita River.

Excessive spring runoff and debris backing up in culverts led to a large sinkhole developing on Highway 133 north of Paonia and south of Somerset, Colorado between mile markers 14 and 19. This resulted in the closure of the highway to allow emergency repairs to be made. The sinking soils were first noticed on April 29, 2023 with the eventual collapse of the highway occurring on May 2, 2023.
Mesonet station (DLCC1) located 7.9 mi ESE of Antelope Lake, CA, and mesonet station (FHDC1) located 2.7 mi SSE of Frenchman Lake, CA, reported 0.65 inches, and 0.88 inches respectively.

Saturated soils from excessive runoff of melting snow lead to numerous mud and debris flows near Glenwood Springs, CO and the near the Hanging Lake Trail in Glenwood Canyon. The mud trapped a train traveling through the west side of Glenwood Springs with no injuries reported. Access to the Hanging Lake Trail was cutoff with roadway closures. Mud also slid off of Red Mountain south of Glenwood Springs, prompting the additional closures of some roadways and a private bridge was washed out.

A COCORAHS (NV-WH-47 Truckee) located 1.0 mi NW of Glenshire-Devonshire, CA, and a CO-OP Observer (FARC1) located 2.0 mi NNW of Floriston, CA, reported 24 hour rainfall totals of 0.43, and 0.48 inches respectively.

An ASOS located at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport, a COCORAHS (NV-WH-2 Reno) located 1.4 mi NNE of Reno, NV, and a COCORAHS (NV-WH-133 Reno) located 1.7 mi WSW of Reno, NV, reported 24 hour rainfall totals of 0.84 inches, 0.91 inches, and 0.93 inches respectively.
A trained spotter located 4.0 mi SSW of Reno, NV, reported a 24 hour rainfall total of 1.04 inches, as well as one inch storm total snowfall.

Rapid snow melt led to high river rises and overbank flooding at and downstream of the junction between the Rio Ojo Caliente and Rio Chama. Ten homes had water come right up to the house structure. This flooded yards, wells and septic tanks. Damages are an estimate.
